chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Ishaq al-Dbabbi, from Abu Imran al-Armani, from Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'There is a group of people, when something from the Quran is mentioned to them or they are narrated it, one of them faints (or screams) to the extent that it is seen that if his hands or his legs were cut off, he would not feel it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! That is from Satan. They are not described by this. Rather, it is softness, tenderness, tears, and trembling.'
Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Imran al-Armani, from Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between spiritual fainting and true reverence during Quran recitation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between genuine spiritual humility and the ecstatic frenzy often attributed to Satan, clarifying that true devotion manifests as softness of heart, tenderness, weeping, and reverent trembling (wajal). This hadith serves as a critical criterion in Shia fiqh of worship for evaluating the authenticity of spiritual states, warning against mistaking sensory overload or demonic distraction for divine proximity. It underscores the balance between emotional intensity and mindful presence during Quranic recitation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Is’haq Al Sabiy, from Abu Imran Al Armany, from Abdullah Bin Al Hakam, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘There is a group of people, when something is mentioned from the Quran or narrated with it, one of them would shriek (scream) to the extent that one of them would view that if his hand or his leg were to be cut off, he would not be aware of that’.

So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! That is from the Satan<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup>, what is attributed with this. But rather, it is the softness and the tenderness, and the tears, and the scruples’.

Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, from Abu Imran Al Armany, from Abdullah Bin Al Hakam, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ya’qub ibn Ishaq al-Dabbiy from abu ‘Imran al-Armani from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam from Jabir who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu Ja’far (a.s.) ‘There are people when remembering something from the Holy Quran or is mentioned before them they suffer a shock to the extent that even if their hands or legs are cut they do not realize.’ The Imam said, ‘Glory belongs to Allah. That is from Satan. That is not how believing people are described. It is only softening, tender feelings, a few tears and anxiety.’”
Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Hassan from abu ‘Imran al-Armani from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) a similar Hadith.
